ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, point D is on $BC$, and $DE\perp AB$ at point E, $AE=AC$. If $BC=4$ and $DE=1.5$, what is the value of $BD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $DE\perp AB$,\\
it follows that $\angle AED=\angle C=90^\circ$,\\
since $AE=AC$ and $AD=AD$,\\
it follows that $\triangle ACD\cong \triangle AED\left(HL\right)$,\\
hence $DE=CD=1.5$,\\
thus $BD=BC-CD=4-1.5=\boxed{2.5}$.

Reasoning: From the given conditions AE=AC, BC=4, DE=1.5. Because E is on AB, AE is a part of AB; also because DE⊥AB, so DE⊥AE. DE is perpendicular to the radius AE, so DE is the tangent to this circle at point E; DC is on BC, and BC⊥AC, so DC is perpendicular to the radius AC, therefore DC is the tangent to this circle at point C.
